poster_title: LLMS' INTERNAL STATES RETAIN THE POWER OF HALLUCINATION DETECTION
authors: Chao Chen, Kai Liu, Ze Chen, Yi Gu, Yue Wu, Mingyuan Tao, Zhihang Fu, Jieping Ye

panels.headline: LLMs often produce factually incorrect or nonsense generations, known as knowledge hallucination.
content: LLMs show impressive abilities in various applications.
Knowledge hallucination is a significant issue in LLMs.
Traditional methods lose semantic information during token-decoding.
Proposed method aims to capture logical consistency in the embedding space.

panels.headline: Token-level uncertainty measures are not effective for entire sequences in modern auto-regressive LLMs.
content: Token-level measures fail to capture sequence-level uncertainty.
Post-hoc semantic measurements are less precise than embedding space modeling.

panels.headline: Propose a generalized INSIDE framework using internal states of LLMs for hallucination detection.
content: Leverage internal states for hallucination detection.
Introduce EigenScore to measure semantic consistency.
Develop test-time feature clipping to reduce overconfident generations.
panels.figure_caption: Illustration of our proposed hallucination detection pipeline. During inference time, for a given question, the extreme features in the penultimate layer are truncated and the EigenScore is computed based on the sentence embeddings across multiple responses.

panels.headline: Achieved state-of-the-art hallucination detection performance on several QA benchmarks.
content: Conducted extensive experiments on QA benchmarks.
Performed ablation studies to verify EigenScore and feature clipping.
panels.figure_caption: Hallucination detection performance evaluation of different methods on four QA tasks. AUROC(AUC) and Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) are utilized to measure the performance.

panels.headline: EigenScore represents differential entropy in the sentence embedding space.
content: Feature clipping significantly improves detection of overconfident hallucinations.
Performance is sensitive to temperature and top-k parameters.
panels.figure_caption: Performance sensitivity to temperature and top-k. The performance is measured by AUROC s.

panels.headline: The INSIDE framework provides a more precise and reliable method for hallucination detection.
content: INSIDE framework leverages internal states for hallucination detection.
EigenScore and feature clipping show significant improvements.
Method is effective but may vary across different LLM architectures and datasets.
Future work includes extending to other LLMs and applications.
